title: Closed vocabularies
description:
Every enumeration this profile closes, in one place. A value outside one of these is refused rather than carried: a vocabulary that admits a free string is a vocabulary a consumer cannot branch on.

`ddd` is carried only where a kind covers several constructs. Where it is absent the kind *is* the construct, and a `ddd` beside it would name one fact twice.

kind.description: Closed at eight and 1:1 with the construct vocabulary the analysis records. Nothing is a field of something else, so nothing loses an identifier by being one.

origin.description: `stated` where the material says it; `modeled` where the analysis decided it. A reviewer accepts the first and disagrees with the second, and can do neither if the two look alike.

gapKind.description: `domain` waits on whoever knows the domain and no capability of this framework may close one. `authoring` waits on the enrichment pass.

subdomainType.description: Where the business differs, where it is merely specific, and where the problem is solved. It decides where careful modelling is worth its cost.

interfaceDdd.description: A `command` is a message a context accepts, and it belongs here because an interface is what a context publishes or consumes. `ownership: consumed` on a command says this context accepts it; `published` says this context sends it to another. A command that is refused never becomes a process, which is why it is not a `processDdd`.

ownership.description: Whether this context exposes the interface or depends on someone else's. It decides who owes whom compatibility.

contextRelationshipPattern.description: `separate-ways` is a real answer: two contexts that do not need each other are not connected because a diagram looks better connected. Four of the seven are directional and carry a `role`; three are symmetric and refuse one.

binding.description: A reference whose target lies in another aggregate declares `by-identity`. How a binding becomes a storage representation is stack knowledge and is not recorded.

relationshipRole.description: What *this* context is relative to the one it names. Upstream decides and owes compatibility; downstream absorbs the decision. Carried only by a directional pattern: a `shared-kernel` has no upstream side, and a `role` beside one would name a fact that does not exist.

consistency.description: Whether this rule holds within one transaction or converges after it. An invariant spanning two aggregates is eventually consistent, and saying so is the difference between a boundary drawn honestly and one drawn wide enough to hide the question.

x-rejected-fields.status: Rejected, not merely absent. A node declares no status, no maturity level and no approval state; an open `kind: authoring` gap is what says a pass has not run.
x-rejected-fields.superseded_by: Rejected. A node that changes kind, boundary or name takes a new identifier and the old one is removed with every reference to it. Version control holds what the base held.

x-directional-patterns.why: A `customer-supplier` with no side named says two contexts integrate and not who owes whom compatibility, which is the whole content of the pattern. A `shared-kernel` has no sides to name.

x-open: `origin` and `gapKind` are stated here **and** by the authority: `schemas/knowledge-notation.json` carries the first as an inline enum on `properties.origin` and the second inside its `gap` shape. Both are envelope fields, so their vocabularies are the envelope's to close, and `tables/envelope.json` opens by saying it restates nothing. These two are the exception nobody declared. The composer drops them from the shipped contract because nothing references them there — so the duplication costs nothing today and the prose beside them, which is this profile's reading and not the authority's, reaches no consumer. Resolving it means either the envelope referencing these definitions or this table losing them, and neither is decided.
